beforeEffective.effectiveText: An RNA-lipoplex is a particle in which RNA is complexed with lipids. Its behaviour depends on the exact lipids, charge balance and route, so a result for one lipoplex does not transfer to another product.

A lipid nanoparticle is a formulated fat-based carrier that protects RNA and helps it enter cells. Getting into a cell, releasing usable RNA into the cell fluid and making protein are separate steps, and a particle can succeed at the first without the others.

Targeted lipid nanoparticles use a surface ligand or a changed lipid mix to favour particular cells or organs. Enrichment in a tissue is not the same as working protein made only in the intended cell type.
